episode.known_final_diagnosis: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a microangiopathy affecting skin and muscle; activation and deposition of complement causes lysis of endomysial capillaries and muscle ischaemia, resulting in a cutaneous rash and muscle weakness.1 This presentation as a paraneoplastic phenomenon has become better recognised in recent years, most commonly with ovarian, lung, pancreatic, stomach and colorectal cancers plus non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. In the majority of paraneoplastic cases, DM precedes the neoplasm.2 We present, here, a rare case of DM diagnosed as a paraneoplastic phenomenon 3 weeks post-diagnosis of human papilloma virus associated SCC of the cervix.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 70s presented with postmenopausal paravaginal bleeding and slowly progressing proximal shoulder weakness. Urgent workup diagnosed stage IIIC squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix with a 5 cm tumor and an internal iliac lymph node. Physical examination revealed characteristic purple/red macular rash over metacarpophalangeal joints, outer thighs, knees, proximal muscle wasting, and marked proximal muscle weakness (MRC 2/5). Routine labs showed raised inflammatory markers but lacked specific muscle enzyme data. Autoimmune serology and muscle biopsy were ordered; serology results were referenced but specific antibody levels were not documented, and biopsy results were unavailable. Despite missing detailed lab confirmation, the clinical presentation and skin/muscle findings strongly support dermatomyositis as a paraneoplastic syndrome arising shortly after cervical SCC diagnosis.
